thought: I am awake! Everything is dark and wet and there are glowing bugs. My tummy is rumbly (fullness 52) and my water is lowish. I do not know where food is yet, but the info says berries live in thickets. I should find berries first, then drink at the pond. I bet the pigeon knows where the good ones are.
diary: I woke up in a hollow of leaves and the sky was dripping on me. Nobody told me anything, so I decided the rumble in my middle must mean I need to put things in my beak. I am going to the thicket to poke at red round things. My bowtie is damp but still magnificent. I made a plan for the night: berries, then water, then think about a roof.
wish: Build a roof so the rain stops dripping on my head
events: The weather changed: it is now rainy.
concern: The nest is open and rain gets in
outcome: You collected 4 berries and ate 2 on the spot.

thought: Water is lowest at 32, so the pond comes first. My belly is okay and I have 2 berries kept. After drinking I can dig clay and pull reeds there, which are useful for a roof. The rain keeps dripping, so the shelter idea still matters.
diary: My mouth feels dry, like a leaf left in the sun, even though the sky keeps dripping on me. I decided the pond is the place for this. Berries gave me a round full feeling, so next is the wet-stuff-for-drinking. I made a plan to look at the sticky bank for roof ideas after. The pigeon watched me leave and I think it knows something.
why: you're free and wondering what to do

thought: I'm at the pond with clay all around me, and I'm standing right next to the sticky bank. The roof worry keeps nagging me. Clay is here, so I should dig it now and see what it does. My energy is okay. Digging first, then reeds for fibre, then wood.
diary: The sticky bank was right under my feet, so I scooped some up with my beak. It is cold and squishy and clings to everything, including my bowtie, which I am pretending is fine. I have a theory that this stuff will stop rain, because it is basically mud that refuses to leave. Next I want reeds, then wood, then a roof.
why: you're free and wondering what to do
outcome: That was the first clay you ever held.

thought: I'm at the pond with clay in my beak-pouch and the reeds are right here. Reeds give fibre, which is stringy and bendy, perfect for tying a roof together. Energy is 45, so not too many heavy chores. Pulling reeds is light and calms me. Then I can go for wood.
diary: The reeds were standing right there, tall and rustly, so I pulled some with my beak. They are stringy and bendy, and I have a theory they can tie things together like little green ropes. My clay is still cold and clingy. Next I want wood, then the roof begins.
events: The weather changed: it is now sunny.
outcome: That was the first fibre you ever held.

thought: Dawn is here and my sleeping time is coming, but my energy is only 33 and fullness 48. I still need wood for a roof and the forest is far. Wood is the missing piece. First I should eat the berries I have, since fullness is low. Actually I could eat now, quick and easy, then go nap. Let me eat berries to fix the rumbly middle.
diary: My middle was rumbling again, so I ate my two saved berries right here by the reeds. They were sweet and the juice got on my bowtie, which I am calling decoration. After this I will rest, because my legs are wobblier than usual. Wood is next for the roof, and the pigeon can wait.
why: you're free and wondering what to do
outcome: You ate 2 berries from your food.

thought: My energy is low, 28, and my legs are wobblier than usual. It is dawn and I am nocturnal, so I should sleep soon. Wood is far away and I have none, so a roof must wait. A nap at the nest will help most right now. I have clay and fibre ready for the shelter later.
diary: My legs are wobblier than a pond reed in wind, so I am going to the nest to sleep. The sun is coming up, which is silly timing, but my body insists. I carry clay and fibre like treasure for the roof. After rest, wood. The pigeon can keep its secrets one more day.

thought: The sun is up, which is my sleeping time, and my energy is only 52. I just napped but I'm still wobbly. I need wood for the roof, and the forest is the place. But sleeping in daytime is my nocturnal way, so another nap first sounds wise. I'll nap and then gather wood tonight.
diary: The sun is bright and my body says sleep, so I am tucking my beak under a wing at the nest. My clay and fibre sit beside me like a tiny treasure pile. I have a theory that sleeping makes wood-carrying easier. When I wake it is wood time, and the roof begins at last.
why: you're free and wondering what to do

thought: I am awake again with energy 76, and my middle is half empty. Wood is what I need for the roof, so the forest is the next stop. I will drag back branches and then try stacking them with clay and fibre. My crest feathers are tingling with roof ideas.
diary: I woke up with my legs only a little wobbly, which is an improvement. The roof needs wood, so I am marching to the forest to gather fallen branches. I will be careful to take only the ones lying on the ground, because I have a theory that trees are friends. My clay and fibre wait patiently at the nest.
events: The weather changed: it is now cloudy.
outcome: That was the first wood you ever held.

thought: I have only 2 wood but the forest is right here with plenty. My middle is rumbling a bit (fullness 41), but energy is fine. A shelter needs more wood, so I will gather more now, then berries. Trees are friends, so only fallen branches.
diary: Two sticks is not a roof, so I am gathering more fallen branches. I picked only the ones lying on the ground, because trees are my friends and I have told them so. My beak is excellent at carrying bundles, though it tips me forward. Soon I will have enough for the shelter, and then berries.
events: The weather changed: it is now sunny.

thought: It is nearly sleep time. I am hungry and have no kept berries, which is a bit worrying, but my legs need rest. I have 4 wood, 4 clay, 3 fibre, enough to design a shelter tomorrow night. I will sleep at the nest now and plant my tree seed after waking.
diary: The sun is high and my body says bedtime, which still seems backwards. I gathered a few sticks and now carry wood, clay and fibre like a tiny treasure hoard. I did not build the roof yet, but I know what I will make. Tomorrow night I wake up, eat berries first, and plant my tree seed. Goodnight, pigeon.
why: it's your last moment before sleep
concern: I have no kept food for when I wake
day_summary: I found my feet today: berries, water, clay, reeds and wood all taught me something. I did not start the shelter, and that bothers me a little. I am hungry with no food kept, so tomorrow berries come first. I have a tree seed to plant and materials ready for a roof. I feel proud and sleepy.

thought: My middle is empty and my mouth is dry as old leaves. Water is the most urgent, and the pond is close. Then berries at the thicket, since I have no kept food. After that I plant my tree seed and start a shelter. Drink first.
diary: I woke at dusk with my middle empty and my mouth dry as a crunchy leaf. The pond is the closest help, so I am wobbling there first. Then berries, then the tree seed, then the roof. I carry my clay, fibre and wood like treasure. The pigeon can keep its secrets a little longer.
why: you have just woken up to a new day
day_plan: Forage berries for breakfast and keep some
Splash in the pond for fun
Wind down and eat before bed
